_fleet_ceiling.rule: Sanaa 2026-09-03 ~21:00Z, the ONE hard limit that survives: "a fleet-wide safety ceiling on any single run (e.g. 3x its registered cost cap, or the box's remaining budget, whichever is smaller) ... at the ceiling the monitor stops the run gracefully regardless of residual trend."
_fleet_ceiling.source: etc/sessions/2026-09-03T2100Z_sanaa_launch_rule.md (committed 825285bb; read at source by this lane, not taken from a relay)
_fleet_ceiling.arithmetic: registered cap 50 core-min x 3 = 150 core-min; at ranks 1 that is 9000 wall s
_fleet_ceiling.term_2_why_null: NOT MEASURABLE FROM THIS BOX. COMPUTE_BUDGET_CHARTER.md section 5: the box cannot read its own billing. The min() is therefore evaluated on term 1 ALONE, and this field is null rather than a guess. If a remaining-budget figure is ever supplied and is below 150 core-min, IT GOVERNS and this ceiling drops to it.
_fleet_ceiling.CEILING_IS_INERT_ON_THIS_ROW_AND_HERE_IS: The registered timeout on this row is 3000 s = 50 core-min at ranks 1, which is EXACTLY 3x STRICTER than the 150 core-min ceiling. The registered timeout therefore binds first and the fleet ceiling is never reached. That is Sanaa's stated intent -- "a ceiling far above the estimate, not the estimate itself" -- and it is recorded so no reader mistakes the ceiling for slack.
_fleet_ceiling.THE_CEILING_AUTHORISES_NO_WIDENING: Writing this ceiling on the row changes NO behaviour and does NOT license raising --timeout toward it. run_one_t19.sh:75 REFUSES any --timeout that is not EQUAL to the registered timeout_s, in either direction, and rule 12 and CLAUDE.md's reserved list put widening a registered cap outside this lane's authority entirely. The ceiling is protection against the box being eaten; it is not a budget to spend up to.
